description: A detailed machine-readable knowledge graph derived from the user-provided Wikipedia article text on overlay networks, with explicit entities, relationships, examples, architectural patterns, trade-offs, and source provenance. Model-expanded illustrations are marked separately from article-stated claims.

limitations: The input is a Wikipedia article excerpt, not a full technical standard.
The source article itself marks some statements citation-needed and includes a promotional-content/neutrality notice.
Examples and architecture patterns added beyond the article are explicitly labeled as model expansion.

data_model.id_policy: Stable namespace-prefixed IDs; relationship endpoints must refer to an entity or an architecture pattern ID.
data_model.source_policy: Source references point to the user-provided article and its bibliography records. Article claims are not treated as independently verified.

entities.name: Overlay network
entities.description: A logical computer network layered over an existing physical or underlay network; the article says the underlay is almost always some form of IP network.

entities.name: Underlay network
entities.description: The existing physical and network infrastructure that transports overlay traffic.

entities.name: Logical link
entities.description: A connection in the overlay topology corresponding to a path through one or more links in the underlying network.

entities.name: Overlay node
entities.description: A participating endpoint or system that forms part of the overlay topology.

entities.name: Logical addressing
entities.description: Addressing that identifies overlay entities or destinations independently of the underlying IP address.

entities.name: Encapsulation
entities.description: Wrapping a payload in one or more protocol headers to carry it through the underlay; adds overhead.

entities.name: Network tunnel
entities.description: A logical path that carries traffic between endpoints using an encapsulating protocol.

entities.name: Quality of Service (QoS)
entities.description: Mechanisms for differentiating traffic treatment and, in some designs, controlling service characteristics.

entities.name: Network resilience
entities.description: Ability to recover automatically from failures or degraded paths to maintain a desired service level or availability.

entities.name: Overlay topology
entities.description: The logical arrangement of nodes and links used by an overlay protocol.

attributes.edges: logical links carried over underlay paths

entities.name: Multicast
entities.description: Delivery of data from one or more sources to a receiver group, with overlay approaches implementing distribution among participating end systems.

entities.name: Peer-to-peer networking
entities.description: A model in which participating peers communicate and may organize themselves into a logical network over existing Internet connections.

entities.name: Distributed hash table (DHT)
entities.description: A distributed data structure that maps keys or logical identifiers to responsible nodes without requiring the requester to know a destination IP address in advance.

entities.name: Traffic engineering
entities.description: Selection or management of paths and traffic treatment to meet application or operational goals.

entities.name: Latency
entities.description: Time taken for traffic or a message to travel through a system; overlay detours may increase it.

entities.name: Bandwidth overhead
entities.description: Capacity consumed by additional headers, encapsulation, relaying, or duplicated traffic.

entities.name: Failure recovery
entities.description: Detection of a network failure or degraded path and selection of an alternative path.

entities.name: Application layer
entities.description: The layer at which applications or overlay software can implement routing, recovery, multicast, or other behavior.

entities.name: IP network
entities.description: A network using Internet Protocol addressing and forwarding; commonly serves as the underlay for overlay networks.

entities.name: Virtual private network (VPN)
entities.description: A logical private network implemented across shared infrastructure; BGP VPNs and IP tunneling are examples of overlays.

entities.name: Software-defined wide-area network (SD-WAN)
entities.description: An overlay WAN approach that adds programmable policy and path-selection flexibility across underlying network services.

entities.name: Network security
entities.description: Protection of overlay traffic and participants through mechanisms such as encryption, isolation, and access policy; the article lists security as an overlay attribute.

entities.name: Encryption
entities.description: Cryptographic transformation used to protect traffic confidentiality and sometimes integrity, depending on the protocol.

entities.name: IP multicast
entities.description: Network-layer multicast capability described in the article as having limited deployment, motivating end-system alternatives.

entities.name: Unicast
entities.description: Delivery from one sender to one destination; overlay multicast topologies commonly use underlying unicast paths between peers.

entities.name: Network layer
entities.description: Layer responsible for network-level packet forwarding; IP multicast is discussed as a network-layer mechanism.

entities.name: Telecommunications service provider
entities.description: An operator that can offer overlay services on top of its physical and IP infrastructure.

entities.name: Data center networking
entities.description: Networking among servers, virtual machines, containers, and clusters in a data-center environment.

entities.name: Enterprise wide-area network (WAN)
entities.description: Connectivity joining geographically separated enterprise sites and applications.

entities.name: OSI layered networking model
entities.description: The conventional layered networking model; the article notes overlay networking is conceptually distinct from traditional OSI layering.

entities.name: Internet
entities.description: The global IP-based network that commonly transports overlay traffic and can itself host multiple logical networks.

entities.name: Telephone network
entities.description: Circuit- and packet-switched telecommunication infrastructure that the article uses to illustrate historical and changing overlay relationships.

entities.name: Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP)
entities.description: Voice communication carried over IP networks; the article notes the telephone network increasingly becomes an overlay on the Internet through VoIP.

entities.name: Network congestion
entities.description: A condition in which demand competes for network resources; DiffServ can influence forwarding priority under congestion but does not itself guarantee throughput.

entities.name: Per-flow tracking
entities.description: Tracking individual flows to apply service treatment; the article identifies scaling concerns for IntServ.

entities.name: IPsec
entities.description: A family of IP-layer security protocols used for protected communications and commonly used in tunneling/overlay designs.

entities.name: Generic Routing Encapsulation (GRE)
entities.description: A tunneling protocol used to encapsulate packets inside other packets.

entities.name: VXLAN
entities.description: A network virtualization overlay technology commonly used in data centers to extend Layer 2 segments over an IP underlay.

entities.name: BGP VPN
entities.description: A provider-operated VPN service using BGP-based mechanisms to connect enterprise sites while isolating enterprise-specific addressing and routing.

entities.name: Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS)
entities.description: A provider network technology mentioned as part of the migration from legacy Frame Relay/ATM enterprise services.

entities.name: Frame Relay
entities.description: A legacy packet-switched telecommunication infrastructure formerly used to carry enterprise private networks.

entities.name: Asynchronous Transfer Mode (ATM)
entities.description: A legacy packet/cell-switching infrastructure formerly used for enterprise private networking.

entities.name: Differentiated Services (DiffServ)
entities.description: A traffic differentiation model widely deployed by operators to classify and prioritize traffic, but not itself a throughput guarantee.

entities.name: Integrated Services (IntServ)
entities.description: A QoS approach requiring per-flow tracking; the article notes scaling issues and limited deployment.

entities.name: Resilient Overlay Networks (RONs)
entities.description: Application-layer overlay architectures whose nodes monitor Internet paths and reroute traffic through alternative overlay nodes to recover from disconnection or interference.

entities.name: Overlay multicast

tradeoff_matrix.benefit: Can identify and route to destinations independently of their currently known IP address.
tradeoff_matrix.cost_or_limit: Requires overlay-level naming, lookup, or routing mechanisms.

tradeoff_matrix.benefit: Can select overlay-node sequence and apply application/site/user-specific policies.
tradeoff_matrix.cost_or_limit: Cannot directly control the underlay's route between two overlay nodes.

tradeoff_matrix.benefit: Can detect path degradation and reroute at the overlay layer.
tradeoff_matrix.cost_or_limit: Still depends on lower-layer availability and may choose a longer path.

tradeoff_matrix.benefit: Can provide logical isolation and optionally encryption.
tradeoff_matrix.cost_or_limit: An overlay by itself does not guarantee confidentiality, authentication, or secure endpoint behavior.

tradeoff_matrix.benefit: Enables logical networks and tunnels over shared infrastructure.
tradeoff_matrix.cost_or_limit: Additional headers consume capacity and can affect MTU/fragmentation behavior (MTU note is model-expanded).

tradeoff_matrix.benefit: Can prioritize traffic by application, user, or site.
tradeoff_matrix.cost_or_limit: DiffServ prioritization does not itself guarantee end-to-end throughput.

tradeoff_matrix.benefit: Can distribute data among peers without relying on router-level IP multicast.
tradeoff_matrix.cost_or_limit: Requires maintaining an overlay topology and may create redundant transmissions.
